subject: Integration & Prompt Governance — SDK, Auth, Routing, Embeddings
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: SDK, auth, routing, prompt governance

Thanks John — great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Summary of needs we heard:
- Integration: ACME wants a lightweight SDK path for server-side calls (Node/Python) and guidance for client-side usage (mobile web).
- Auth: preference for mTLS for high-security endpoints, SSO for admin console access; want options for API keys scoped per service.
- Routing & availability: route by latency-first for US web traffic, fallback to lower-cost model variant for burst traffic; can also pin critical routes to Dedicated.
- Outputs: need structured outputs + function/tool calling for inventory lookups and order status; deterministic JSON schema preferred for downstream services.
- Embeddings / reranker: plan to embed product catalog (≈1.2M docs); want recommended vector size and batch strategy; reranker to re-rank top-K candidates.
- Prompt governance: ask about versioning system prompts, mitigations for prompt injection, and red-team process to validate guardrails.

Attachments: acme-architecture-draft.png, prompt-governance-checklist.pdf (attached).

Proposed next steps (owners and timeline):
1) Tech deep-dive (Marcus + Dev) — detailed SDK auth & routing demo, sample embedding pipeline, and function-calling schema. (Owner: Marcus) — schedule this week if possible.
2) Share SDK snippet + auth patterns (Marissa) — include Node + Python examples and mTLS notes. (Owner: Marissa) — deliver by EOD tomorrow.
3) Prompt governance starter template & red-team plan (Marcus) — include versioning recommendations (git tagging, immutable prompt ids) and injection test checklist. (Owner: Marcus) — draft in 3 business days.
4) Action plan + procurement kickoff for Dedicated capacity options (Laura) — include cost estimate. (Owner: Laura) — coordinate with procurement.

Can you confirm which auth approach your security team prefers (mTLS + scoped API keys vs organization-wide API keys + SSO), and availability for a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive?

Thanks,
Marissa

- Embeddings: for our catalog, what embedding dimensionality do you recommend? We currently use 1536 for other vendors. Also: how do you recommend handling periodic revectorization (monthly vs event-driven)?
- Reranker: we expect to retrieve top-200 candidates from the vector DB and then apply lightweight MLP reranker before final scoring — would that align with Redwood patterns?

- Prompt governance: curious about immutable system prompt IDs and whether Redwood supports prompt signing or checksums to detect drift or unauthorized edits. Also want to understand your red-team process and whether we can run an initial injection test in a staging environment.

Subject: RE: Post-call recap + next steps: SDK, auth, routing, prompt governance

John — thanks for the questions. Short answers up front, then details and sample snippets.

1) Embedding dimensionality & revectorization
- 1536 is a valid choice and widely used; if you want smaller payloads and similar quality, 1024 can work with quantization. Given 1.2M docs and monthly change rate ~5%, we recommend monthly batch revectorization with incremental updates for high-traffic items. Use sharded batch jobs (500–1k docs per job) to avoid long-running tasks.

2) Reranker flow
- Typical pattern: retrieve top-N (200) from vector DB → lightweight reranker (MLP or small transformer) re-scores top-50 → final re-ranking using context-aware generation for the top-5. This aligns with Redwood reference arch and gives best balance of throughput vs accuracy.

3) Auth patterns & SDK setup
- For high-security endpoints (PII), we recommend mTLS for service-to-service. For client apps, use short-lived scoped API keys minted via your auth service (OIDC + client credential flow). Admin console integrates with SSO (SAML/OIDC).
- Attached is a small SDK snippet bundle (sdk-auth-sample.zip) with Node and Python examples. Key notes in snippet:
  - Node sample: use Node SDK with certificate pinning for mTLS + fallback to scoped API key for batch jobs.
  - Python sample: demonstrates embedding batch upload with async batching and backoff.

Node pseudocode (inline):
```
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({
  mtlsCert: fs.readFileSync('client.crt'),
  mtlsKey: fs.readFileSync('client.key'),
  baseUrl: 'https://api.redwood.example',
});
// scoped key fallback for batch jobs
await client.authenticate({ type: 'scoped_key', key: process.env.ACME_EMBED_KEY });
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.createBatch({ items: docs });
```

4) Routing & model variants
- Routing policy options: latency-first (lowest p99 within region), cost-aware (prefer quantized model variants), and pinned (explicit model id). We support policy DSL in route configs. For bursts, set autoscale + fallback to a quantized compatible model to maintain throughput.

5) Structured output & function/tool calling
- Recommend explicit JSON schema and function signatures. Example function call we use for order lookup:
  - function name: check_order_status
  - params schema: { order_id: string, include_items: boolean }
  - expected return: { order_id, status, eta_iso, escalation_flag }
- Use tool calling to keep LLM deterministic; validate schema server-side after call.

6) Prompt governance (versioning, injection mitigation, red-team)
- Versioning: store system prompts in a git repo with semantic version tags (v1.0.0), plus immutable prompt IDs in metadata. Keep a change log and require PR reviews for prompt changes.
- Signing: add a checksum (sha256) and store checksum in prompt metadata; validate checksum at deploy time to detect unauthorized edits.
- Injection mitigations: enforce input sanitization, strict JSON schema validation for outputs, and use guardrail prompts that explicitly reset context before executing sensitive instructions. Use separate models/endpoints for untrusted user text vs system-level prompts.
- Red-team: run an automated suite of injection tests (open redirect, nested instructions, malicious payloads) in staging with a canary model; track failures in a prompt-regression dashboard and block prompt changes that increase failure rate.

Drive link with sample schemas and deeper docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-acme-sdk-snippets (attached in thread).

If Wed 10–12 PT works, Marcus and Dev can join. We’ll prepare the SDK snippets and a short demo deck (20–30 min) focusing on embeddings pipeline and function-calling safety.
